plain: In October 1962 the United States set off a nuclear bomb high above Johnston Atoll, a tiny island in the Pacific, in a test called Bluegill Triple Prime. Harold Malmgren, who is described as an adviser to four presidents, says the test report stated that the blast knocked down a "device", and that the Navy recovered it after it fell into the ocean. He says he was refused more information, went to Albuquerque to see for himself, and held the pieces in his hands. If true, something unknown was watching a nuclear test, and the US government kept what fell. A man named Kurt McConnell says Malmgren was told directly by a man named Richard Bissell that a UFO watching the test had been downed by accident. A researcher, Jeff Cruickshank, says the recovery shows up in the ships' deck logs, the daily records a ship keeps, and that a spherical piece of debris with unusual properties was found. A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, says he co-wrote that deck-log study, though he calls it only a partial recovery of the object or something related to it, and Ross Coulthart cites an analysis by Douglas Dean Johnson that he says backs Malmgren up. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells the story across many episodes, and the tellers differ mostly on who Malmgren's source was and how much was recovered.
